headline: Warm, dry Friday with highs in the mid to upper 70s, then a weak, light-rain system Saturday and cooler weather.
summary: As of Thursday evening, high pressure aloft keeps western Washington dry and warm through Friday, with highs in the mid to upper 70s and fairly dry afternoon air (relative humidity in the upper 30s to low 40s percent). Tonight, east winds turn breezy, mostly in the Cascades and nearby foothills, with gusts likely 25 to 30 mph, and they ease by Friday morning. Because air is flowing from land toward the water, fog should be limited, though isolated patchy fog is still possible in the south Sound and in fog-prone valleys. Winds return to blowing in from the ocean Friday afternoon, and a weak front crosses Saturday. Most lowlands should get only a few hundredths of an inch of rain, the Cascades around a quarter inch, and parts of central Puget Sound possibly even less because of a rain shadow. Westerly winds pick up Saturday afternoon and evening in the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Admiralty Inlet. Sunday looks cool and mostly dry, with highs in the upper 50s and low 60s. A low-pressure system arrives Monday, but most models track it south of western Washington, so Monday should be dry and cool; this is less certain, since not all models agree and the discussion's opening summary mentions rain early next week. Another weak front may bring isolated showers Wednesday into Thursday.
changes: Early discussions called for dense morning fog, with an advisory extended to 10 AM, and for more widespread rain on Saturday; later ones said fog would clear, Friday fog would be limited, and Saturday's rain would be light. Monday and Tuesday shifted from unsettled then dry to dry but cool Monday, with a weak midweek front bringing only isolated showers.
